article.content: Software giant reports $36.6bn in profit, beating Wall Street expectations, as Azure cloud computing division grows 48% Microsoft gained billions of dollars in stock market value Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, just days after it offered voluntary buyouts to some 60,000 employees. The office software giant’s growth was fueled by its Azure cloud computing division, which grew by 48% in the September quarter. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Technology conglomerate Microsoft generated **$92.3 billion** in revenue during its latest quarter, according to figures published by Business | The Guardian, outperforming analyst projections on Wall Street. The report states that the software giant accumulated **$36.6 billion** in profit for the period. Market reaction followed the financial disclosures on Wednesday afternoon, lifting the company's valuation by billions of dollars.

## Strong Cloud Expansion and Workforce Shifts

The robust quarterly performance was driven largely by the corporation's infrastructure sector. According to Business | The Guardian, the **Azure** cloud computing division expanded by **48%**. This upward trajectory aligns with prior disclosures highlighting how [Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/microsoft-recorded-billion-in-revenue-from-openai) and earlier milestones where [Microsoft hits 10 quarters of record-breaking revenue in a row](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/microsoft-hits-quarters-of-record-breaking-revenue-in-a-row). 

Simultaneously, the source notes that the company offered voluntary severance buyouts to **60,000** staff members, marking a major workforce restructuring effort running parallel to its financial growth. 

## Broader Industry Trends

Large technology firms have increasingly balanced aggressive capital expenditures in artificial intelligence infrastructure with cost-control measures across their traditional business segments. While enterprise cloud adoption continues to accelerate globally, corporate leadership teams face mounting pressure from investors to streamline headcount and demonstrate operational efficiency even amid record top-line expansion.

## Why This Matters

This simultaneous push toward massive cloud expansion and deep workforce restructuring illustrates the shifting priorities of the technology sector, where massive investments in artificial intelligence and infrastructure require significant capital redirection. For workers, these moves highlight a persistent vulnerability even within highly profitable corporations, while shareholders closely monitor whether headcount reductions can sustainably fund next-generation computing systems.

## What to Watch

Market analysts will monitor upcoming filings for further details regarding the uptake of the employee buyout packages and the exact composition of the Azure division's financial contributions. Observers will also track whether the **48%** growth rate in cloud computing sustains its momentum through the upcoming fiscal quarters amid fluctuating macroeconomic conditions.

Sources: [Business | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/28/microsoft-earnings)
